question: Should OpenClaw adopt local, container, reverse-proxy, and node-mode as the initial named, release-tested hosting-profile catalog over the separate readiness framework?
rationale: The PR intentionally creates new profile-selection and support-contract surface; source review cannot determine whether this is the product boundary maintainers want to own in core.

options.title: Approve the four-profile v1 catalog
options.body: Accept the proposed opt-in catalog, contingent on landing the readiness dependency and obtaining exact-head packaged conformance proof for the linked core implementation.

options.title: Defer named profiles
options.body: Accept or continue the general readiness work independently and revisit profiles after real deployment support requirements are established.

options.title: Narrow the initial catalog
options.body: Approve only the postures maintainers are ready to support and defer proxy or node-mode contracts to focused follow-up RFCs.

recommendation.title: Approve the four-profile v1 catalog
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed opt-in catalog, contingent on landing the readiness dependency and obtaining exact-head packaged conformance proof for the linked core implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current profile design and the dependent readiness proposal, so they are best placed to incorporate the resulting scope decision.
